title: Five model families have a cross-family SST radiation gain above one in 1980-2014
abstract: We tested whether the large radiation response to AMIP-minus-HighResMIP SST differences is shared across model families. We used the signed monthly aggregates from seven model pairs, averaged related resolutions into five families, and removed cubic time and sea-ice terms. A covariance ratio that excludes same-family products gave a radiation gain of 2.34 relative to the five-model Green's-function mean. The descriptive 95% three-year block interval was 1.47-3.00. The gain was 2.49 without volcanic years and 2.06 from 1985. Removing any one family left gains above one. A three-family subset with small clear-sky trend differences gave 1.93 (1.04-2.71). Both clear-sky and all-sky-minus-clear-sky radiation covaried with the predictor. Total shared residual covariance remained uncertain. Under independent family noise, the result supports a shared predictor-aligned excess rather than only independent atmosphere noise. Shared forcing differences and related model physics can also give this signal. These exploratory in-record estimates do not establish a causal SST artifact effect or a transferable correction multiplier. No new model runs or observations were used.

display.caption: Cross-family gain and residual covariance in five family means. Bars are descriptive 95% synchronous three-year block intervals with controls refitted.
